description: The bar chart illustrates a comparison of four reasoning methods—CoT, CoD, CCoT, and CoUT—across two metrics: Accuracy (%) on the left y-axis (ranging from 70% to 100% in 5% increments) and Token Count on the right y-axis (ranging from 0 to 800 in 100-unit increments). Each method is represented by a pair of adjacent bars: the left bar in each pair shows Accuracy (%) and the right bar shows Token Count, with color-coded legends at the bottom identifying CoT (red), CoD (orange), CCoT (light blue), and CoUT (green). CoT achieves the highest accuracy at 91.19% with a token count of 676.85; CoD has 80.89% accuracy and 534.24 tokens; CCoT scores 88.50% accuracy with 445.91 tokens; and CoUT attains 88.40% accuracy using only 354.46 tokens. The chart visually emphasizes that CoUT offers a favorable trade-off, achieving near-top accuracy with the lowest token consumption, while CoT, though most accurate, is the most token-intensive. The bars are grouped by method and not sorted by value, allowing direct side-by-side comparison of performance and efficiency for each approach.
